title: S020 — Decision provenance / minimum sound invalidation
description: Determine the minimum information required to decide whether a previously established Phase A judgment remains valid after an intervention.
result_summary: BLOCKED. A per-node decision-rule provenance (negated | forced | support | unfounded) is observable deterministically and explains every S019 divergence, but the rule-level invalidation predicate is NOT sound: FN=32, FP=0, invalidated=0 (negateEvent 26, retractFact 3, severEdge 2, forceEvent 1). Every false negative comes from the SUPPORT rule: to know whether a support-established TRUE still holds, the predicate must re-evaluate the support, which is precisely Phase A. Minimum-information analysis: Level 3 (deciding rule) is the richest level capturable without semantic work, and it is unsound; the minimum SOUND witness for support-decided nodes is effectively the derivation itself (Level 5). Shadow-engine audit: sound invalidation requires class D (reimplementation of propagation semantics) - the shadow engine the brief forbids.

answers.Q1_evidence: one of three rules decides a Phase A node: negated (FALSE), forced (TRUE/FALSE), support (factNodeTruth/hardSupport); Phase B can reject via unfounded
answers.Q2_dependency_provenance_sufficient: NO - it does not say which support actually decided the node
answers.Q3_additional_provenance: the deciding rule, plus for support the winning group AND its conjuncts current judgments (the last part is the derivation)
answers.Q4_or_without_duplication: NO - OR/disjunctive support cannot be handled without re-evaluating the groups = Phase A
answers.Q5_force_negate_override: YES - handled correctly by structural accumulator checks
answers.Q6_cycles: need the Phase B unfoundedSet result; unfounded provenance is conservatively safe (no FN) but cannot make a positive determination without re-running Phase B
answers.Q7_granularity: per node for the rule; but support decisions also depend on the conjuncts judgments, so a node-local record is insufficient
answers.Q8_minimum_sound_witness: deciding rule + (for support) the current support evaluation - i.e. the derivation; no cheaper sound witness found
answers.Q9_state_per_judgment: rule-level ~1 small value per node; a SOUND record is effectively the full support graph + current judgments
answers.Q10_engine_can_record: the rule-level record CAN (done); a SOUND witness CANNOT without class-D logic
answers.Q11_basis_for_incremental: not yet - incremental Phase A needs support re-validation, which is the engine

next_experiment: either incrementalise WITHIN Phase A (accept support re-evaluation as the local operation), or find a support representation cheaper to re-check than to recompute.
limitations: Seed canons + 200-step random histories; OR/AND/ENABLES/cycle cases were reasoned through the three deciding rules rather than built as synthetic graphs (budget).
Only the rule-level witness was implemented; Levels 4-5 were characterised, not implemented.
Long-horizon, branch, determinism measurements not run (predicate disqualified).
